**Starts** once #244 is merged.

## Why

An agent evaluation sets up a real moment from a past session, and scores what the coordinator does next. This issue builds the setup: a command that starts a run from any turn of a recorded session, and runs that one turn on today's code.

With turn 4 as the example, a run gives the coordinator:

- **Turns 1 to 3 as they were recorded,** with every user message, reply, and tool call with its result. The SDK loads them from the copied transcript when it resumes the session, the same way every normal turn works. Nothing in them runs again.
- **The trip as it stood when turn 4 started,** from its trip version (#243).
- **A turn 4 message,** either the recorded one or a new one.

The coordinator does its turn 4 work, and what it says and saves can be scored. The conversation and the trip stay fixed, so only the instructions, the tools, or the model change between runs. Running turns 1 to 3 live instead would drift, since the coordinator answers a bit differently each time.

#53 builds the evaluations on this: the datasets, the scorers, and the experiments in Phoenix. This issue covers only the setup and the one turn.

## Design

- #243, for what a trip version holds, and #244, for the Bar Harbor versions.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 6 (sessions and transcripts), 8.5 (sessions, and the line the app adds on a resume), and 8.9 (trip versions, and how tooling finds a turn's message in the transcript).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2, for the app's lines on each message.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 6 and 10, for reaching the server's Postgres and Phoenix through an SSH tunnel.
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.3, for how the #132 spike ran a conversation for a fresh user through the same code as `npm run chat`.

## Decided

- **The source is a session on the live database,** read through the SSH tunnel. The run itself is on the local stack (systems design, section 6), and its trace goes to the server's Phoenix, as for any local turn.
- **Personal data stays in the databases.** Nothing from a recorded session goes in the repo. Tests use made-up data.
- **The command takes the agent session ID, the turn number, and the message:** the recorded one, or new text.
- **Each run gets a fresh test user, trip, and session.** It copies the transcript lines before that turn's user message, workers' lines included. Workers run only inside a coordinator turn, so in `transcript_lines.id` order, every worker line from an earlier turn comes before the turn's message. So the cut is every row, coordinator or worker, whose `id` is below that message's row. It also copies the trip version from that turn's start: the plan, the places, trip memory, and user memory. IDs inside the trip stay the same, since the conversation names them. To find that turn's user message, use `turnMessageIndex()` in `src/agent/shown-messages.ts` (#247), on the coordinator's lines in `id` order. It gives the message's place in that list. It counts user messages the same way the trip version's turn number was counted. It throws if the message there doesn't end with the words the version saved. So a run can't pair a version with the wrong moment. Versions saved before #247 have no saved words, so the function refuses them.
- **A place's key is its trip and its ID, and a memory item's key is its user and its ID.** Decided by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat. Today `places.id` and `memory_items.id` are each unique in the whole table. A run keeps the recorded IDs, so its copy would clash with the recorded rows, and with any earlier run of the same session. In the local database, the Bar Harbor trip from the version rebuild (#244) already holds them. Every lookup already gives the trip or the user, apart from `PlaceRepository.fillNames()`, which gets the trip added. Sharing one place row between trips was the other choice. It would need a table linking trips and places, and memory would still need copying, since a run can change or forget a memory item. A migration changes the two keys, and the persistence design says so.
- **The turn runs through the same code as `npm run chat`,** with today's instructions and tools.
- **The command prints the new user, trip, and session IDs, and the reply,** so a scorer can read what was saved.
- **Each run leaves its test user's rows in the local database.** That's fine for a local database, as in the #132 spike.
- **The coordinator can't tell a run from a real session.** Nothing it sees may differ from what it would have seen in the recorded turn, apart from the turn itself and Claude Code's date (below). The message gets exactly the recorded turn's app lines, and the app adds none of its own, such as a resume line. A new message keeps the recorded lines, with only the user's words replaced.
- **The trip's date comes from the app's line, not from Claude Code.** Decided by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat, in place of running Claude Code with a fake clock:
  - **The app's date line names the trip.** Today it says "Today is Sunday, October 10, 2027." (technical spec 5.2), which reads like Claude Code's own "Today's date is 2026-10-27." It changes to something specific to planning the trip, such as "For planning this trip, today's date is Sunday, October 10, 2027." This changes the line on the live site too.
  - **The coordinator's instructions say to plan by that line.** Any rule that uses today's date, such as the start date, the forecast, or the trip's start, goes by the date in that line, even if another date shows up.
  - **A run's date line has the recorded turn's date.** Recorded messages have the old wording, so the copy rewrites each old date line into the new wording, with the same date.
  - **The app's own clock uses the recorded turn's time,** which is the trip version's `saved_date_time` (#244 sets it from the turn's message line), for code that uses today's date, such as the weather tools and the started-trip check. The tool servers already take a `now` function.
  - **Claude Code's date is left alone.** On the live site it already matches the app's line, since #194 runs the Claude Code process in the trip's time zone. In a run, it's today's date, and on resume Claude Code adds "The date has changed. Today's date is now ..." ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.9). That's the one accepted difference from a real session. If runs show the coordinator reacting to it, it gets looked at again.

## Open questions

- ~~Which app lines does the turn's message get? The app adds lines to each message, such as today's date (technical spec 5.2), and a line saying the session was resumed (persistence design 8.5). The recorded turn has the lines it ran with. A copied session looks like a resume to the app, so it would add a resume line the recorded turn may not have had, and today's date. Proposal: the recorded message is sent exactly as the model got it, app lines included, and the app adds none of its own. A new message keeps the recorded turn's app lines, with only the user's words replaced. Code that checks dates, such as a forecast window, still uses today's date. That's accepted, since the gap is a few weeks.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-02, in chat: the coordinator must not be able to tell a run from a real session. So the message gets exactly the recorded turn's app lines, and the app adds none of its own. A new message keeps them, with only the user's words replaced. For the date, see Decided.

## Do

- Check first that the SDK resumes cleanly from copied lines. If the lines name the old agent session ID, or the copy needs anything else rewritten, rewrite it in the copy.
- Check whether the copied transcript names the old trip, session, or user ID anywhere the coordinator or its tools would use it. Rewrite any that would break the run.
- Change the app's date line, and add the rule to plan by it, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Update `withoutAppLines()` in `src/agent/app-lines.ts` to strip the new date line, and keep it stripping the old one. Live sessions recorded before this change keep the old wording, and the chat view still has to hide it. Add a test for each wording.
- Write the command, outside `npm run check`.
- Write how to use it into DEVELOPMENT.md section 5.

## Done when

- A run that starts the Bar Harbor session at turn 5, with the recorded message, gives the coordinator the same trip it saw in the recorded turn 5: its first read in the turn matches the recorded one, apart from format. The coordinator answers, and the turn's trace is in Phoenix.
- The same works with a new message.
- Nothing in the run tells the coordinator it isn't the recorded session. Check the run's transcript: after the copied lines, it has nothing the recorded turn didn't have, such as a resume line, apart from the turn itself and Claude Code's date change line. If needed, check a model call's full input with a logging proxy, as #188 did.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
